items.title: Manny Albam interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998
items.q: In the band was Shorty Rodgers, let me see, the trombone player DeVito, Eddie Bert, a whole bunch of all young kids in the band.

ctx.x: Can you recall the first thing that you wrote for somebody, and hearing it back?

Yeah. We had a band up in the Bronx. I didn’t live in the Bronx but I used to go to the Bronx to play with these kids and we were high school people, I think I was 16 or 17. In the band was Shorty Rodgers, let me see, the trombone player DeVito, Eddie Bert, a whole bunch of all young kids in the band. Lenny Hambro, who wound up playing with Gene Krupa for years and years, a great alto player. And we were all kids. And somehow or other I wrote a chart on the Pepsi Cola jingle. “Pepsi Cola hits the spot.” And every…

time I used to run into Shorty Rodgers, 50 years later, he wound sing the end of the bridge [scats], which is very strange. That was our greeting. He’d look at me and go [scats]. Memory. I think memory has a lot to do with musicality. I can remember things that I heard in those days, I can remember things I heard yesterday too, but I mean I’ll go back to solos that I played and still remember them, little parts of charts that really hit me. Oh also in the band was Stan Getz as a youngster, a lot of very good…

items.title: Eddie Bert interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001
items.q: in that band I met Shorty Rodgers, Stan Getz, Manny Albam, all these guys were playing in the band.

ctx.x: Sure. A Pullman type? © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

Yeah. And they’d disconnect us and connect us with another train and all that. So we did a whole bunch of theaters. Mildred did some of them with us. But Jimmy Durante was part of the act, until the draft started getting through to the band. So then Red broke up and wanted to get a small band. So he said I don’t have any trumpet player that knows how to play small band, you know in the big band it was different. So I said yeah, I know a guy.
